**Dispatch on T3.** Every subagent is a `delegate_task` call from the chat that runs the playbook, same model family included, so every child shows up in T3. Give each call its own `clientRequestId`, stable across retries of that call, and keep each returned `taskId`. A child's completion wakes this thread, so end the turn instead of polling, and call `task_status` only when a result is needed mid-turn. `task_cancel` stops a child, and `task_status` confirms it stopped. A child gets only its brief, never your context, so pass absolute paths. `<plugin root>` is the absolute path of the directory that holds this plugin's `skills/` and `agents/`. A persona (`poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko`, `thermo-nuclear-review-subagent`, `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review-subagent`) is a brief that opens with "Read `<plugin root>/agents/<name>.md` in full and act as it says", and a `poteto-agent` brief also names this file's absolute path.

A child starts in your checkout. One that writes gets its own worktree, created with `git worktree add` from `HEAD` so it builds on your branch's commits. The brief names that absolute path as the only place it writes, and tells it to run every command there (`workdir` on Codex) and to edit by absolute path. Record your own `git status --porcelain` before you dispatch, check after the result that it is unchanged, then remove the worktree and its branch. A step a playbook says to delegate goes to `delegate_task` on that role's sheet entry, not into your own tool calls, unless you state a reason such as a step too small to brief. A research delegate no role names runs on the `how explorer` entry. A model's family is the first segment of its ID's last `/` part, such as `claude`, `gpt`, or `grok`, whatever provider instance serves it, and your own family is the one in `orchestrator_capabilities`' `inheritedModel`. A rejected target runs on another target of the same family from `orchestrator_capabilities`, and you say so. A required review with no reviewer from another family stays `BLOCKED: independent review`.

End every reply that ran a playbook with a dispatch ledger: one line per delegated step, naming the role and the `providerInstanceId/model` it ran on, or `in-thread: <reason>`.
substitutions.rationale: inserts the T3 dispatch policy at the end of the Subagents section (Tool actions; Subagent policy)

substitutions.pattern:
```bash
ls -t <agent-transcripts>/*.jsonl <agent-transcripts>/*/*.jsonl <agent-transcripts>/*/subagents/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | head -10
```

That covers the legacy flat (`<id>.jsonl`), current nested (`<id>/<id>.jsonl`), and subagent (`<parent>/subagents/<child>.jsonl`) layouts. For each candidate, read the first JSONL line. Take the file whose `message.content[0].text` contains the conversation's opening user prompt. If none matches, pass a tight digest of the session instead.
substitutions.replacement:
On Claude Code, run the finder with this session's ID, this project's transcripts directory, and a fragment of the conversation's opening user prompt:

```bash
node "<plugin root>/skills/reflect/scripts/find-transcript.mjs" --session "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID" "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/<encoded-cwd>" "<opening prompt fragment>"
```

`<plugin root>` is the directory that holds this plugin's `skills/`, and `<encoded-cwd>` is what `node -p 'process.cwd().normalize("NFC").replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-")'` prints in the directory Claude Code started in, which is that directory's physical path with every character other than an ASCII letter or digit turned into `-`. If the result is longer than 200 characters, Claude Code keeps the first 200 and appends `-` and a hash, so use the folder under `projects/` whose name starts with those 200 characters and that holds this session's transcript. With the session ID set, the finder prints this session's own transcript, and exits 1 when it does not exist, because a scan could return a sibling session that shares the opening prompt. Without it, the finder scans the flat, nested, and subagent layouts newest first and prints the first transcript whose opening typed prompt carries the fragment. Do not reimplement the scan by hand.

On Codex, pass this thread's ID, which Codex exports as `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, to the resolver, and never search by chat title or time:

```bash
"<plugin root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/resolve-codex-transcript" "$CODEX_THREAD_ID"
```

On success it exits 0 and prints JSON whose `path` is the transcript. If either command exits non-zero, pass a tight digest of the session instead.
substitutions.rationale: Transcripts (t3-pstack 1.0.13: find-transcript.mjs on Claude Code, resolve-codex-transcript on Codex)

substitutions.pattern: Run `drive` and `background` under `/loop` in dynamic mode.
substitutions.replacement: Run `drive` as a loop inside the turn: run the watcher with `--timeout 540` and the shell's own timeout above 540 seconds and under the 600-second tool cap, act on its verdict, and run it again. Report and stop when the verdict's head SHA, kind, and reason have not changed for two hours, or after three hours in all. A `BLOCKER` with reason `review-required` or `merge-blocked` (exit 6) needs a person, so report it and stop the loop instead of rerunning the watcher. `review-required` is the wait for a human review below, and `merge-blocked`, a branch protection rule the watcher cannot name, goes back to the user. Run `background` by arming T3's `watch_pull_request` on the frontier and taking the watcher's verdict with `--timeout 180` at each natural pause. A wait for a human review is `watch_pull_request` and the end of the turn, because another account's review wakes the thread. Unwatch with `unwatch_pull_request` when babysitting stops. The watcher holds `READY` until accounts other than the PR author and the `gh` viewer have been quiet on the PR for `--settle` seconds (default 300) since the latest push, opening, or ready for review, and up to 30 minutes after that while an `eyes` reaction is open, so no per-bot wait rules are needed.
substitutions.rationale: Playbooks: Babysit drive and background; the watch-pr settle overlay (t3-pstack 1.0.5); the exit 6 merge gates from pstack-claude #95 (t3-pstack 2.0.0-rc.2)
